messages.author: f87814d7c9410bb4
messages.subject: DSM estimating over-abundance
parts:
Hello,

I am running DSM for two season data (Summer and Winter) for ungulate species. Detection function is estimating higher detection probability in Summer probably due to larger cluster size and increased visibility. When moving forward with this to spatial abundance estimation using DSM, it is highly over-estimating the abundances. 
Model parameters were then corrected for influential observations, smoothers wiggliness. Model details are the following:

Summary of uncertainty in a density surface model calculated
 analytically for GAM, with delta method
Approximate asymptotic confidence interval:
       2.5%        Mean       97.5% 
   66298.34  2098572.22 66427079.21 
(Using log-Normal approximation)

Point estimate                 : 2098572 
CV of detection function       : 0.1115305 
CV from GAM                    : 4.62 
Total standard error           : 9698296 
Total coefficient of variation : 4.6214 

I figured out a few probable causes for this:
1. larger cluster size variation in Summer (correction for this did not help much)
2. High detection probability 
3. Model is predicting high abundance in the non-sampled area that have similar covariate values as those segments where sightings have occurred.

I do not understand what else could cause this and how to correct this?
I would be more than happy to share more details on this.

Many Thanks and Regards,
Deepti Gupta

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] DSM estimating over-abundance
parts:
Deepti

Sounds as if you may have extrapolation issues arising from unusual covariate combinations in some of your non-sampled grid cells.  Could be the case that a small number of grid cells are contributing to the massive abundance estimates.

It isn't simple to determine where those situations arise, but there has been some work done on trying to identify such situations.  I suggest you have a read through this St Andrews technical report:

Bouchet , P J-F , Miller , D L , Roberts , J , Mannocci , L , Harris , C M & Thomas , L 2019 , From here and now to there and then : practical recommendations for extrapolating cetacean density surface models to novel conditions . CREEM Technical Report , no. 2019-1 , University of St Andrews .

available online at https://research-repository.st-andrews.ac.uk/handle/10023/18509

This may help isolate some of your problems.

messages.author: 3c8299ac8234f5d2
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] DSM estimating over-abundance
parts:
Hi Deepti,

The error you're getting is likely related to an issue with the coordinate system being used.  I note that your function call is given an aftt_crs object, which I imagine was taken directly from the package vignette. This is unlikely to be appropriate for your study system, unless you are working in some area of the southeastern United States. I would recommend using a relevant CRS for your study area and seeing if that helps. 

Please also check that the specified CRS matches the coordinate units in both the segments and prediction.grid objects. I was able to reproduce your error by having (x,y) coordinates in lat/lon format within the segments / prediction.grid data.frames, but using a mismatched (projected) coordinate system (e.g., with units of metres like in aftt_crs).

The warning messages that were returned in the console are intentional, and were built in to the package to make users aware of some of the things that are happening under the hood. In your case, the locations in prediction.grid are not regularly spaced (which is required to get a raster), so dsmextra automatically generates rasters based on the resolution you specify, and lets you know this is what it's done. Note that the resolution argument is typically a single number, so if you want a 200 x 200 m raster then you should only write resolution = 200.

The second warning is now deprecated in the latest version of the package (v 1.1.1) and should no longer appear. You might want to grab that version off Github as we've made a number of minor adjustments to functions throughout, in part to accompany the paper we recently wrote about the package (available here in pre-print form: https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/2041-210X.13469).

If you're still struggling after trying the above, I am happy to liaise with you off-list to solve the problem. 
We can then report back to everyone with a solution.

Best

--
Phil Bouchet

Centre for Ecological and Environmental Modelling
University of St Andrews

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] DSM estimating over-abundance
parts:
Hi listfolks,

I've have liaised with Deepti off-list regarding the above, and thought I would report back.

Part of the issue was that the technical report available here (https://research-repository.st-andrews.ac.uk/handle/10023/18509) pointed to an older version of the code, which is now obsolete.
An updated version (v2.0) of said report has now been uploaded to the St Andrews University Research Repository (same link as above), with the correct links.

Please note that the package website (https://densitymodelling.github.io/dsmextra/) and the associated Github repository (https://github.com/densitymodelling/dsmextra) remain the primary and most up-to-date resources on dsmextra.
Users are encouraged to download and install the latest development version of the package from Github before use.

Additional issues also occurred when attempting to install the package on a mac machine, as a result of unstable dependencies.
A patch has been released today on Github (https://github.com/densitymodelling/dsmextra/releases/tag/v1.1.2) to address these.

Best wishes,
Phil
